articles.title: China quiere evitar que la guerra de precios pueda comprometer la seguridad de sus coches
articles.standfirst: Pekín obliga a los fabricantes a revisar la calidad de sus vehículos después de una oleada histórica de llamadas a revisión que afecta a Tesla, Xiaomi, Xpeng o Geely.
articles.summary: Pekín obliga a los fabricantes a revisar la calidad de sus vehículos después de una oleada histórica de llamadas a revisión que afecta a Tesla, Xiaomi, Xpeng o Geely.
articles.body: China no quiere que la intensa guerra de precios que se vive en su mercado automovilístico tenga consecuencias para los usuarios. Las autoridades del gigante asiático han anunciado una campaña con la que, a lo largo de los próximos doce meses, buscarán mejorar la calidad y la seguridad de los automóviles de fabricación nacional, llamando a las marcas a preparar planes "proactivos" de retirada de aquellos vehículos en los que se encuentren defectos. Así lo anunciaron esta semana en un comunicado conjunto los ministerios de Industria y Tecnologías de la Información, Seguridad Pública, y Ecología y Medio Ambiente, así como el regulador nacional de los mercados, la Administración Estatal para la Regulación del Mercado (SAMR, por sus siglas en inglés). El documento se publica apenas unos días después de que la SAMR anunciase, el pasado 21 de agosto, la mayor orden de llamada a revisión de la historia del país: según la prensa especializada, afectó a más de 7 millones de vehículos de marcas conocidas como Tesla, Xiaomi, Leapmotor, Xpeng, Chery, Geely, Dongfeng o FAW. Precisamente Tesla, empresa estadounidense dirigida por Elon Musk fue la más afectada del grupo, con más de 5,7 millones de automóviles llamados a revisión por defectos en los mecanismos de las manetas de las puertas o en los sistemas de asistencia a la conducción. La iniciativa oficial llama a los fabricantes a revisar "la consistencia, la fiabilidad y la durabilidad" de sus vehículos y a enviar a las autoridades los informes resultantes, incluyendo las medidas tomadas para resolver los problemas detectados, antes de que termine el presente año. Asimismo, deberán "someter a pruebas y verificar las nuevas tecnologías" aplicadas a los automóviles. La campaña busca "mejorar la consistencia, calidad y niveles de seguridad generales del sector, mantener un orden de mercado justo y competitivo y promover el desarrollo saludable y sostenible" de una industria sumida en una prolongada guerra de precios ante los problemas de demanda a nivel nacional, que han hecho que las marcas chinas encuentren en las exportaciones una vía de escape. De hecho, esa coyuntura que las autoridades califican de "competencia irracional" acarrea "riesgos de que la consistencia y la seguridad de los productos decaigan, afectando al desarrollo de alta calidad del sector automotriz", indicó en un comunicado separado la patronal Asociación de Fabricantes de Automóviles de China (CAAM). Justo después del comunicado gubernamental, la CAAM anunció también una campaña propia para "llamar a todas las empresas del sector a respetar los mínimos aceptables de seguridad, consolidar los cimientos de la calidad y la seguridad, estandarizar la innovación tecnológica y reforzar la verificación y las pruebas de los diseños innovadores de productos". Ese mismo día, la Oficina Nacional de Estadística (ONE) divulgó cifras oficiales que apuntaban a que los beneficios del sector automotriz se habían desplomado un 20 % interanual hasta julio, en parte debido a los mencionados descuentos agresivos, que han provocado la intervención de Pekín en varias ocasiones.

articles.title: Alberto Ginés escala hasta un histórico oro europeo en Laval
articles.standfirst: El extremeño se corona campeón continental de dificultad, una gesta que hasta ahora no había logrado ningún español. Es su tercera medalla europea
articles.summary: El extremeño se corona campeón continental de dificultad, una gesta que hasta ahora no había logrado ningún español. Es su tercera medalla europea
articles.body: Alberto Ginés vuelve a tocar el cielo. El número 1 del ranking mundial de escalada de dificultad sigue escribiendo nuevas páginas doradas en la historia del deporte español. Tras su oro olímpico en Tokio 2020 con 18 años en el estreno de este deporte en los Juegos, el extremeño se ha proclamado este domingo campeón de Europa en el rocódromo del Espace Mayenne de Laval (Francia), una gesta inédita en el deporte nacional hasta hoy. Y lo ha hecho con una exhibición. Es su tercera medalla europea tras la plata en Edimburgo 2019 y el bronce en Múnich 2022. Nada más lograr el oro, Alberto sonreía y levantaba el puño derecho. Ya en el suelo, llegaba el grito que sacaba fuera lo vivido estos años y respiraba hondo. Después volvía a sonreír. Porque este oro llega tras una travesía por el desierto del extremeño, que llegó a odiar la medalla olímpica porque al mirarla le hacía sentirse un impostor. Tardó tres años en volver a ser él mismo. En París 2024 acabó séptimo lastrado por una lesión en un pie. Su sequía dorada duró cinco. Llegaron las dudas y empezó a pensar que quizás no estaba destinado a ganar hasta que se impuso en la Copa del Mundo de Chamonix el mes pasado. Era su tercer podio esta temporada de las cuatro pruebas que había disputado en la modalidad de dificultad (plata en Wujiang (China) y en Innsbruck (Austria), en la que se ha centrado en su camino hacia Los Ángeles 2028. Este domingo, Ginés comenzó la jornada imponiéndose en las semifinales (44+), por delante del checo Adam Ondra (42+) y del francés Sam Avezou, que defendía la plata europea de 2024. En la final, el español mostró una tranquilidad y un dominio increíbles para escalar hasta el oro (40+), mientras que el italiano Giovanni Placci fue plata (36) y Avezou, bronce (33+). En categoría femenina, Iziar Martínez acabó octava (30) en la final en la que la belga Heloïse Doumont se proclamó campeona europea (52), la eslovena Lucka Rakovec fue plata (51+) y la checa Tereza Siruckova (46). Ginés, de 23 años, ha dejado esta temporada el CAR de Sant Cugat tras ocho años en Barcelona. Necesitaba un cambio y eso ha implicado no sólo la mudanza a otro país (Eslovenia) sino dejar atrás a David Maciá, su técnico desde hace 13 años y actual responsable del módulo de escalada del CAR barcelonés. Ahora se entrena en un grupo de trabajo liderado por Roman Krajnik, el mismo entrenador de Janja Garnbret, la escaladora más laureada de la historia (oro en Tokio 2020 y París 2024 y con 12 medallas mundiales). A diferencia del CAR de Barcelona, los entrenamientos son siempre en pared, no hacen gimnasio.

articles.summary: ESPAÑA - ALEMANIA: 0-0 (Q2 - Min 1) Ya estamos en el segundo cuarto. La defensa de medio campo española está muy bien plantada y provocando el fallo a
articles.body:
Última hora del España - Alemania de la final de hockey 2026 en directo:

España afronta hoy uno de los partidos más importantes de su historia. Los RedSticks se enfrentan a Alemania , actual campeona del mundo, en la f inal de la Copa del Mundo 2026 . El encuentro comenzará a las 16:30 horas en el Belfius Hockey Arena de Wavre (Bélgica).

La selección masculina de hockey disputará la tercera final mundialista de su historia y la primera desde Utrecht 1998. Los RedSticks ya fueron subcampeones en Barcelona 1971 y en la cita neerlandesa de hace 28 años, pero todavía buscan conquistar su primera Copa del Mundo. En su último duelo por el oro, España llegaba consagrada tras conquistar la plata olímpica en Atlanta 1996 ; en esta ocasión, el bloque que dirige Max Caldas es un equipo emergente que sin embargo ha demostrado que ya está para competir por todo.

Enfrente estará Alemania, vigente campeona mundial. Ambos equipos ya se encontraron en la segunda fase del campeonato , en un partido que terminó con victoria española por 2-1 gracias a un doblete de José 'Chefo' Basterra.

Durante este torneo, España inició la primera fase con una victoria por 3-1 frente a Sudáfrica, perdió por la mínima ante Australia (0-1) y aseguró su presencia entre los ocho mejores con otro triunfo por 3-1 contra Irlanda . La segunda fase los RedSticks la iniciaron con la citada remontada ante Alemania y después empató 1-1 con Bélgica . En semifinales llegó una de las mayores gestas de la historia del hockey español. El combinado nacional derrotó por 4-3 a Países Bajos, campeona olímpica y anfitriona, después de remontar el tanto inicial de Koen Bijen. ' Chefo' Basterra firmó un hat-trick , Pepe Cunill completó la goleada y Luis Calzado volvió a resultar decisivo bajo los palos.

articles.title: Patriots reportedly waive defensive tackle Eric Gregory ahead of NFL roster deadline
articles.summary: The NFL’s 53-man roster deadline arrives at 6 p.m. ET Sunday.
articles.body:
A claim from last August will be returning to the wire.

The New England Patriots have waived defensive tackle Eric Gregory ahead of the NFL's 53-man roster deadline, as first reported Sunday by ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Gregory, 25, landed in Foxborough on the heels of the 2025 cutdown deadline after spending his rookie preseason with the Cincinnati Bengals. The 6-foot-3, 319-pound undrafted free agent out of Arkansas went on to appear in seven games, including the AFC wild card, before being placed on injured reserve later in the playoff run. Across 136 snaps on the interior defensive line, he had a hand in eight tackles while providing nose depth.

During last week's preseason finale against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field, Gregory started and stayed in for 56 percent of the workload. That marked the highest rate among non-linebackers and defensive backs in the fold.

The reigning AFC champions went from 91 to 73 reported players on the eve of the NFL's deadline and acquired running back Corey Kiner in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals.

When factoring in designations to return from injured reserve, plus the physically unable to perform and non-football injury lists, active rosters around the league will be down to 53 by 6 p.m. ET Sunday.

articles.title: Rashod Bateman Faces Charges After Assault Claim Recanted
articles.summary: Marissa Crumley says the Ravens receiver never put his hands on her, but Bateman still faces three charges and an NFL personal conduct review.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman is facing three criminal charges stemming from an alleged June domestic dispute, but the mother of his child later withdrew a central accusation that he physically assaulted her. Marissa Crumley told a prosecutor five days after the incident that Bateman never pushed her into a wall or otherwise put his hands on her, contradicting the account initially documented by police.

Bateman was arrested June 3 following an early-morning argument at the couple's Georgia home. According to the police report, Crumley initially alleged that Bateman pushed her into a corner wall during a dispute over a previous relationship and ordered her to pack her belongings.

Investigators said the conflict later continued at another location, where Bateman allegedly struck the windows and a tire of Crumley's Mercedes with a screwdriver. The couple's 3-month-old daughter was inside the vehicle at the time.

Police said broken glass left cuts on Crumley's face. Emergency personnel reportedly found no visible injuries on the infant, though both Crumley and the child were taken to a hospital for evaluation. Bateman was subsequently charged with family violence battery, reckless conduct and felony property damage.

The allegations also triggered an NFL review under the league's personal conduct policy, which allows the league to impose discipline regardless of the outcome of a criminal case.

In a June 8 email that she authorized Bateman's attorneys to provide to TMZ , Crumley said she wanted prosecutors to hear the "true side of the story."

She claimed officers pressured her to identify Bateman and lifted her head wrap to photograph marks on her face, an action she characterized as an invasion of her privacy.

Crumley said those marks were self-inflicted during a moment of emotional distress. "He did not push me or put hands on me in any way," she wrote, adding that she made false statements because she was upset and wanted Bateman "in trouble."

Crumley also said she and Bateman are not violent toward each other, remain in love, and want to create a healthier situation for their daughter. Her revised account specifically disputes the alleged wall shove, although the available reporting does not indicate that she withdrew the allegations involving damage to the Mercedes.

Bateman's attorney, Jordan Siev, previously said the matter had been taken "completely out of context for sensational reasons." He added, "We will let the court process play out, and the facts will come out at that time."

The case arrives as the Baltimore Ravens prepare for a season in which Bateman's availability could affect their receiving corps. The former first-round draft pick appeared in 13 games during an injury-limited 2025 campaign, recording 19 receptions for 224 yards and two touchdowns.

If you or someone you know is experiencing domestic violence, confidential help is available through the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 800-799-SAFE (7233), by texting START to 88788, or at TheHotline.org. In an immediate emergency, call 911.

articles.title: Lazio make official Hutchinson offer to Leicester City, push Dia and Ratkov out
articles.summary: Lazio have made an offer for Leicester City striker Lorenz Hutchinson, while they try to send Boulaye Dia to Rennes and Petar Ratkov to Levante.The Aquile ar...
articles.body:
Lazio have made an offer for Leicester City striker Lorenz Hutchinson, while they try to send Boulaye Dia to Rennes and Petar Ratkov to Levante.

The Aquile are in action this evening with their second Serie A game of the season against Genoa, but meanwhile the club directors are working round the clock to give coach Gennaro Gattuso a suitable squad.

BOLOGNA, ITALY – AUGUST 24: Gennaro Gattuso, Head Coach of Lazio, looks on before the Serie A match between Bologna FC and SS Lazio at Stadio Renato Dall'Ara on August 24, 2026 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

According to GIVEMESPORT , a proposal worth £1m has been made to buy Leicester City forward Hutchinson, even though he is yet to make his senior debut for the club.

He scored 15 goals in 15 games for the Under-18 Premier League side last season, and played for England at Under-19 level.

The deal isn't quite done yet, as they are still discussing the terms, including a sell-on clause.

ROME, ITALY – MAY 17: Boulaye Dia of SS Lazio competes for the ball with AS Roma goalkeeper Mile Svilar during the Serie A match between AS Roma and SS Lazio at Stadio Olimpico on May 17, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Sky Sport Italia report that the Biancocelesti are in the process of releasing two other forwards abroad.

Dia is eager for a move to Stade Rennais, but while the player has agreed personal terms, the two clubs continue to discuss both the financial aspects of the deal, and even more crucially the formula involved.

It remains to be seen if they'll work out a loan with option or obligation to buy.

VERONA, ITALY – JANUARY 11: Petar Ratkov of SS Lazio during the Serie A match between Hellas Verona FC and SS Lazio at Stadio Marcantonio Bentegodi on January 11, 2026 in Verona, Italy. (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

The same source also notes that a loan has been agreed for Ratkov to join Levante in Spain, although the forward still has to discuss personal terms.

It is set to be a loan at €1m with option to buy for a further €14m.

articles.title: Aaron Donald's contract looms over his potential return
articles.summary: If the two sides can't reach a deal as to what he'd be paid, things could get very interesting.
articles.body:
As the potential Aaron Donald unretirement deliberations continue, some have pointed to his contract as a potential impediment. If it is, no one is saying anything to give credence to that dynamic.

Here's how the situation works. Donald's retirement mothballed the remainder of his prior deal: one year, $30 million.

The Rams currently have $16.7 million in cap space . The day Donald returns to the roster (if/when that happens), his $30 million will hit the cap. By 4:00 p.m. ET on that day, the Rams would need to create at least $13.3 million in cap space.

Whatever the magic number for 2026, it would be very easy to restructure his pay. They'd give him a large chunk of it as a signing bonus and add voidable years to the deal, pushing the excess cap charge into future years and significantly reducing his 2026 cap number.

But cap space is only part of the calculation. Cash is the other. All teams have spending budgets. Most are set before the league year begins. And $37 million went to Myles Garrett in early June, on top of the various commitments previously made to the other players on the team.

Receiver Puka Nacua, who clearly deserves a new deal, will eat up more of that money if/when the Rams extend a low-money rookie contract that expires after the coming season.

Donald's possible return has hovered for weeks. Surely, the Rams have planned for all relevant contingencies. Since June, however, the market for defensive tackles has moved to $38 million, thanks to the Jalen Carter deal in Philadelphia.

Donald won't, and shouldn't, play for peanuts. He has significant value, and he hasn't been bashful in the past about trying to get it. He held out deep into August in both 2017 and 2018. He mused about retirement after the Rams won the Super Bowl, before the Rams ripped up the three remaining years on his contract and gave him a massive increase.

Yes, work will need to be done if Donald returns. Quickly. The Rams would need to have a plan in place for finalizing a new contract on the day he officially returns. In theory, they potentially would have to cut him and re-sign him, if a deal can't be buttoned up by 4:00 p.m. ET.

It's possible that the two sides have discreetly reached a consensus as to how a new contract would be structured, and that they've agreed to keep it quiet while Donald continues to assess whether he'll play. If they haven't, the Rams have at least fully strategized a plan as to how they'd wave the cash-and-cap wand in order to absorb Donald's contract in a way that checks all boxes.

It's also possible that the real reason for the delay is the contract, and that everyone involved realizes that keeping their mouths shut about it is the only play. It's not a crazy thought; Donald wouldn't want to create the impression that he's being greedy (despite the fact that he has every right to expect to be fairly compensated), and the Rams wouldn't want to create the impression that they could have added Donald to a team that's already the betting favorite to win the Super Bowl but that ownership was too cheap to close the deal.

And here's where things could get downright nutty. If Donald, through his process of working out intensely for nearly three months in an effort to come back, shows up and refuses to renegotiate his contract, the Rams would either have to quickly come up with $13.3 million in cap space elsewhere or get him off the roster by 4:00 p.m. ET on the day he's reinstated from the reserve/retired list.

To complete this unlikely-but-not-impossible hypothetical scenario, Donald could be released by the Rams if he won't relent on his $30 million — and then become a free agent. He'd be able to hit the open market. And any other team, from the Seahawks to the 49ers to the Cowboys to the Patriots to the Broncos to the Texans (that possibility will make offensive coordinators pee a little), could try to sign him.

As fascinating as the possibility of Donald being available to any other contender may be, the Rams surely have a plan in place to account for the possibility that Donald would show up, Brett Favre-style, and say, "Deal with my $30 million cap number." Still, if the Rams' plan consists of regarding the move as a bluff and calling it, Donald could potentially (and the chances are slim but not zero percent) make his comeback with another contender that is willing to pay him considerably more than the Rams would offer.

articles.title: Cardinals acquire former Rams TE in trade with Jaguars
articles.summary: The Cardinals are bringing Hunter Long back to the NFC West, acquiring the former Rams tight end from the Jaguars.
articles.body:
Hunter Long is back in the NFC West. On Sunday, the Jaguars traded Long to the Arizona Cardinals , the second time in his career that he's been traded.

The Los Angeles Rams originally acquired Long in 2023 as part of the Jalen Ramsey trade that sent the All-Pro cornerback to Miami. Long, a 2021 third-round pick by the Dolphins , spent two years with the Rams before signing with the Jaguars in 2025 free agency.

He signed a two-year, $3 million deal with Jacksonville last offseason but will now try to make an impact in Arizona behind Trey McBride.

In two years with the Rams, Long caught just seven passes for 60 yards. Last season in Miami, he caught 12 passes for 85 yards and two touchdowns, the first scores of his career.

articles.title: Penn State a Large Favorite Over Marshall in Season Opener
articles.summary: It’s game week!
articles.body:
Week 0 is in the books. It was a big day for former Penn State quarterback Beau Pribula, who helped lead Virginia to a 34-8 thumping over conference foe NC State. Charles Huff, part of James Franklin's initial staff as running backs and special teams coach, also had a hot start with a victory over UNLV.

But now, we turn our attention to the Nittany Lions as they prepare to make their season debut on Saturday. Penn State is currently a 24.5-point favorite over their week one opponent, the Marshall Thundering Herd.

Huff led Marshall to a Sun Belt championship in 2024, but the team suffered a decline in 2025 under new head coach Tony Gibson, finishing just 5-7. There is some reason for optimism for a bounce back year, especially as the Herd were able to hold on to the highly-productive Carlos Del Rio-Wilson at quarterback.

Penn State and Marshall will kick off at 3:30 p.m. Saturday in Beaver Stadium, with coverage provided by FS1.

articles.title: ACC Football Power Rankings: Virginia, UNC impress in Week 0
articles.summary: Five ACC football teams competed in Week 0, with some impressing and others struggling. Here are the updated ACC Power Rankings.
articles.body:
The 2026 college football season is here, and five ACC teams competed in Week 0.

The Miami Hurricanes enter the season as the clear best team in the conference and are looking to win their first conference title since joining the league in 2004. While they are the favorites, they will have some some competetion with the SMU Mustangs and Louisville Cardinals also expected to compete for the conference title.

None of the league's top teams competed in Week 0, but the Virginia Cavaliers and North Carolina Tar Heels both picked up impressive wins. The Cavaliers crushed the NC State Wolfpack 34-8, securing the first ACC win of the season. North Carolina's win wasn't as emphatic, but they managed to grind out a 15-10 victory over the TCU Horned Frogs in Ireland.

The FSU Seminoles and Stanford Cardinal also opened the season with wins. Stanford scored the final 14 points to hold on and beat Hawaii while FSU struggled to pull away from New Mexico State, raising several questions about them.

With the season underway, here are our ACC power rankings after Week 0:

Boston College has never gotten going under head coach Bill O'Brien, and he needs to show signs of progress after going 2-10 in Year 2. They made some intriguing transfer additions, but it could be another long season for the Eagles.

So many things went wrong for the Orange last year, with them going 3-9 after several quarterback injuries. Steve Angeli is back and should stabilize the position, but he is returning from an Achilles injury, and that is always concerning.

NC State entered the 2026 season looking to make some noise in the ACC, but failed to do anything in Week 0, getting crushed by the Virginia Cavaliers on the road. CJ Bailey was just 12 of 23 passing for 84 yards and an interception, also fumbling it away once.

FSU got the win in Week 0 over New Mexico State, but it was far closer than it should have been. The offensive line struggled throughout the game, forcing running backs Samuel Singleton Jr. and Ousmane Kromah to bail them out. Mike Norvell's seat is scorching hot, and the win did nothing to cool it off.

The Cardinal have struggled ever since joining the ACC, but Tavita Pritchard started his tenure off with a win over Hawaii. It will likely be a tough season, but it was a perfect start to the season for them.

Bill Belichick did not impress in his first season as North Carolina's head coach, but the Tar Heels look much improved to start Year 2, picking up a 15-10 win over the TCU Horned Frogs. Time will tell just how much better they are, but they looked like a much better-coached team.

Jake Dickert led Wake Forest to nine wins a year ago and will look to keep it going in Year 2. They have a talented quarterback in Gio Lopez, but had to replace large parts of the roster through the transfer portal.

Duke won the ACC in 2025, but is a prime regression candidate after losing quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Cooper Barkate, among others. Manny Diaz is a good coach, but do not expect the Blue Devils to repeat as conference champions.

Mason Heintschel is back at quarterback and will look to take another step as a sophomore. The defense returns several starters and should once again be a physical group.

California brought Tosh Lupoi home, and he aced the offseason, retaining promising quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele. While the offense will rely on JKS taking another step, Lupoi has things trending upwards.

Georgia Tech faces the difficult task of replacing quarterback Haynes King and both coordinators. Michigan running back transfer Justice Haynes should keep the running game humming as Alberto Mendoza takes over at quarterback.

James Franklin will be looking to make an impact in his first season at Virginia Tech, and he has the roster to make some noise. The long-term projection for the Hokies is excellent, with Franklin looking to get them back to competing in the ACC quickly.

Clemson once again enters the 2026 season with one of the most talented rosters in the ACC on paper, but the question is if they can put it together. Last season was a disaster for head coach Dabo Swinney, and he needs to have a good season to show he can still compete in the modern landscape.

Tony Elliott's fourth season was a massive success for Virginia, with the Cavaliers making it to the ACC Championship Game. They are replacing a lot of pieces, but looked excellent in their Week 0 win over NC State, running all over the Wolfpack.

Jeff Brohm went into the portal to get Ohio State quarterback Lincoln Kerholtz, and the Cardinals enter the season as an extremely dangerous team. If running back Isaac Brown can stay healthy, the offense should be improved, putting them in the conference's second tier with SMU.

The Mustangs are looking to make it back to the playoffs and have the roster to make it happen. Quarterback Kevin Jennings is one of the most experienced quarterbacks in the country and has SMU hoping to challenge Miami for the conference title.

Miami made it all the way to the national championship game last year and upgraded the quarterback and wide receiver positions over the offseason. While they have new players stepping up at both lines of scrimmage, they are the clear top team in the ACC.

articles.title: Buccaneers to release Jake Browning; Jalon Daniels set to be No. 2 QB
articles.summary: The Buccaneers gave undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels a shot to win the backup quarterback job and he took full advantage of it.
articles.body:
The Buccaneers gave undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels a shot to win the backup quarterback job and he took full advantage of it.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that the Bucs are going to release Jake Browning as they set their initial 53-man roster on Sunday. Word of Connor Bazelak's departure came on Saturday and that leaves Daniels as the only quarterback behind Baker Mayfield in Tampa.

Browning signed with the Bucs this offseason after spending five seasons with the Bengals. He started three games last year after Joe Burrow was injured, but the Bengals traded for Joe Flacco to fill out the rest of Burrow's time out of the lineup. That starting experience could make Browning an option for other teams looking to change up their quarterback depth chart in the coming days.

Daniels spent six seasons at Kansas and he wrapped up the preseason by going 8-of-15 for 57 yards on Friday night.

articles.title: Live updates: Tracking J.J. McCarthy rumors on Vikings cutdown day
articles.summary: McCarthy's future with Minnesota is murky after presumably falling to QB3 behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy's fall from grace in Minnesota has been astonishing to witness. The timeline has been madness.

Drafted 10th overall in 2024 to be Minnesota's franchise QB

Throws for 188 yards and 2 touchdowns in his preseason debut

We learn the next day that he suffered a torn meniscus that ended his rookie season

Debuts in 2025 and leads the Vikings to a come-from-behind win at Soldier Field in Week 1

Looks awful in a Week 2 loss to the Falcons and suffered a high ankle sprain that knocks him out for the next five games

Returns to lead the Vikings over the Lions and reveals his in-game alter ego, "Nine"

Struggles in four straight losses and is concussed in Week 12 at Green Bay

Misses a week and returns to torch the Commanders and Cowboys in Vikings wins

Sustains a hairline fracture in Week 16 against the Giants and missed another game

Loses alleged QB competition to Kyler Murray

Dings ankle in 2026 preseason loss to Ravens; doesn't play in preseason finale with the QB2 job on the line

Now, with the Vikings' 53-man roster due by 5 p.m. Sunday, McCarthy's future is a mystery. We're going to be tracking rumors all day, so check back frequently for updates.

Dolphins a team to watch in McCarthy rumors

After trading Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Saturday, the Dolphins reportedly cut Cam Miller on Sunday morning. That leaves them without a No. 2 quarterback behind Malik Willis. Could they be making moves before acquiring McCarthy from Minnesota?

The only remaining QB on Miami's roster is former South Dakota State and Iowa star Mark Granowski, who certainly isn't ready for a backup job as a rookie.

Insider doesn't think McCarthy makes the team

Alec Lewis, a very respected beat reporter covering the Vikings for The Athletic, didn't include McCarthy on his final 53-man roster prediction.

"McCarthy's rough week added further murkiness about his status for 2026," Lewis wrote . "McCarthy's comfort (or lack thereof) with being QB3 could dictate his future in Minnesota."

articles.title: Union Berlin close in on preferred Mauro Lustrinelli target Kastriot Imeri
articles.summary: Union Berlin are reportedly closing in on the signing of Swiss attacker Kastriot Imeri from Young Boys Bern, with head coach Mauro Lustrinelli poised to reun...
articles.body:
Union Berlin are reportedly closing in on the signing of Swiss attacker Kastriot Imeri from Young Boys Bern, with head coach Mauro Lustrinelli poised to reunite with one of his former players. According to Kicker , only final details remain before Imeri completes a move to the German capital. The 26-year-old is expected to undergo his medical on Monday before signing a contract through June 2029. Union are reportedly set to pay approximately €2.5m for his services.

Imeri would become the latest Swiss reinforcement for a Union squad that has undergone significant late-window work. The Köpenickers recently completed the signing of Switzerland international Michel Aebischer , adding much-needed quality to a midfield that appeared seriously short of options earlier in the summer.

Get German Football News highlighted Union's need for attacking reinforcements in our 2026/27 tactical preview . Imeri, comfortable cutting inside from the left wing or operating centrally, provides precisely the type of technically gifted and unpredictable option that Lustrinelli's squad previously lacked in the final third.

Lustrinelli set to reunite with former pupil

Imeri is no stranger to the new Union trainer. Lustrinelli previously worked with the attacker at FC Thun, where Imeri registered six goals and eight assists during the club's surprise championship-winning campaign. The Swiss-Italian coach also handed Imeri his Switzerland U21 debut, with contact between the pair reportedly having remained intact ever since.

The move therefore hands Lustrinelli one of his preferred targets as he continues rebuilding Union's footballing identity. After Saturday's 3-3 draw with Eintracht Frankfurt, the 50-year-old described his work in Köpenick as akin to "building a house" , stressing that mentality and team spirit constituted the foundation upon which more developed footballing principles could eventually be constructed.

Imeri should eventually offer Lustrinelli another important piece of that project, though Union will have to wait briefly before deploying their prospective new signing. The Young Boys attacker is currently recovering from thigh problems and is not expected to return to action for approximately two weeks.

Chelsea were under pressure against Brighton after conceding two second half goals, and Xabi Alonso's reaction told us everything.

If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Everything was under control as Chelsea led Brighton 3-0 going into the second half, but we then saw the most recent example of how easily the Blues crumble.

They surrendered all control and conceded twice against the Seagulls, who suddenly smelled blood. We've seen this story play out time and time again in the last few years. All eyes turned to the sideline to our new manager.

Alonso changes swing game back in Chelsea's favour

One thing is for sure – he's not held back. His instant reaction to the 3-2 goal was not one, not two, but THREE changes at the same time, followed shortly by a fourth

The Blues had never had much midfield control, and it was time to change that, Reece James and Moises Caicedo joined the action from the bench, replacing midfield pair Malo Gusto and Romeo Lavia .

In defence, Wesley Fofana dropped out with Josh Acheampong replacing him on the right hand side of the back three.

After that Jorrel Hato also went into the back three with Levi Colwill going off and Pep Chavarria coming on. That injection of fresh energy paid off right away.

Chelsea started the game really strongly with two early goals that set them on their way.

Chelsea's decision to sign and then start Emi Martinez today shows that their new manager has a ruthless side, some are saying.

articles.summary: Newport County boss Hayden Mullins hailed his side remaining unbeaten at Rodney Parade after The Exiles salvaged a late draw against Tranmere on Saturday.  T...
articles.body:
Newport County boss Hayden Mullins hailed his side remaining unbeaten at Rodney Parade after The Exiles salvaged a late draw against Tranmere on Saturday.

Trailing 2-1, Shaquille Gwengwe rescued a point with a 90th minute strike, meaning Newport have taken four points from their opening two home fixtures this season.

In the 2025-25 campaign, they lost 13 of their 22 league games at Rodney Parade, amassing just 22 points as they battled to survive relegation.

After the game, Mullins was asked about his desire to make his home ground a "fortress".

"Yeah, it's big. It's big for us," he replied.

"I think the one big positive is us scoring last in the game and drawing the game. It still feels like we've got something out of the game and we've got to take that.

"We are unbeaten at home. The fans have helped today, the boys have come off the bench and everyone's helped."

Newport now have two away games, at Salford and Northampton, before hosting Fleetwood Town on 12 September.

"It's a real, real big plus and a bonus that we're unbeaten at home, and we've got to use that. We've got to use it as fuel and really strive to make this place a real tough place to come."

articles.title: Pakistan to meet King Charles after Lord's controversy
articles.summary: Pakistan will have an audience with King Charles this week, days after a threat to cancel their tour of England was made because of an interview with the son...
articles.body:
Pakistan will have an audience with King Charles this week, days after a threat to cancel their tour of England was made because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan.

During lunch on day one of the second Test, Sky Sports aired an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran.

Imran Khan has been in prison for the past three years on charges of corruption, which he denies.

Before the interview was aired, the Pakistan Cricket Board raised the prospect of not resuming the second Test at Lord's and cancelling the remainder of the three-match series.

At the time, the England and Wales Cricket Board took government advice from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

Buckingham Palace has confirmed the King is expected to meet the tourists later this week in an engagement planned before the series began.

"His Majesty the King, as Head of the Commonwealth, will receive the Pakistan Men's Test Cricket Team for an audience in the gardens of Clarence House, in the break between the second and third Test matches hosted in England over the summer," said a statement.

It is understood His Majesty will spend around 15 minutes with the Pakistan team.

Legendary all-rounder Imran Khan, 73, had a 21-year international career for Pakistan and famously led his team to World Cup glory in 1992.

He served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022 and was jailed a year later.

In December of last year, Imran Khan's sister appealed to King Charles in his position of head of the Commonwealth to speak out on the situation.

According to The Times, Aleema Khanum said: "Pakistan is a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.

"Its key principles in the charter are rule of law, democracy, and human rights. A member nation is busy destroying all three fundamental principles.

"Member states, especially where King Charles is the head of the Commonwealth organisation, don't speak out against fascism or military dictatorship? What is the point of just organisations then?"

The chairman of the PCB, Mohsin Naqvi, serves as interior minister for the current Pakistan government. The PCB has been contacted for confirmation Naqvi will be present for the audience with the King.

Before the interview with Khan's sons aired, Sky received a complaint, yet pressed ahead with airing a version of former England captain Michael Atherton's conversation with Suleiman and Kasim.

In the interview, Suleiman and Kasim expressed concerns over the treatment and security given to their father, as well as criticising the UK government's response.

Despite the controversy caused by the interview, the Pakistan team returned to the field as scheduled after lunch on the opening day of the second Test.

At the close of play on the second day, Pakistan coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said he and his team did not know about the interview.

"I don't know anything. I'm just focusing on the match," said Sarfaraz. "You're talking about the interview? We don't know about the interview."

In October, England will tour Pakistan for a one-day tri-series against the home side and Sri Lanka.

It will be England's fourth separate tour of Pakistan in the past four years following a 17-year gap between visits to the country because of security concerns.

articles.title: Patriots Cut First External Addition Of Offseason In Roster Surprise
articles.summary: The Patriots’ first outside addition of the offseason appeared to have a path onto the roster, but New England’s young linebackers changed the equation.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots ' first outside addition of the offseason will not make it to Week 1.

New England released veteran outside linebacker Jesse Luketa as part of its initial wave of roster cuts, according to Mark Daniels of MassLive . The decision came less than six months after the Patriots signed Luketa to a one-year contract.

Luketa was not a headline-grabbing acquisition, but his combination of NFL experience and special teams ability appeared to give him a legitimate path to the 53-man roster.

Instead, the Patriots moved on before Sunday's 6 p.m. ET deadline.

That makes Luketa one of the more surprising names among the team's early cuts.

Jesse Luketa Brought Experience To Patriots

Luketa entered the NFL as a seventh-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals in 2022. The Penn State product appeared in 31 games over three seasons with Arizona, making three starts. The 6-foot-3, 253-pound defender recorded 35 tackles, three sacks and one forced fumble during his time with the Cardinals. All three of those sacks came during the 2024 season.

Luketa also played extensively on special teams, an area that typically gives reserve linebackers an advantage during roster competitions.

After leaving Arizona, Luketa spent part of the 2025 season on the Los Angeles Rams' practice squad. He did not appear in a game before New England signed him March 5, making him the Patriots' first external addition of the 2026 offseason.

That early investment did not guarantee him anything under Mike Vrabel.

Luketa recorded three tackles in New England's 37-13 preseason loss to the Cleveland Browns, but he failed to produce a sack, takeaway or other defining play during the preseason.

Patriots' Younger Linebackers Gain Ground

Luketa's release offers another indication of how New England views its younger options on the edge. The Patriots selected Gabe Jacas in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft and added Quintayvious Hutchins in the seventh. They also drafted Namdi Obiazor in the sixth round to strengthen the second level of their defense.

Jacas started all three preseason games after returning from the non-football injury list, while Obiazor led New England with 11 tackles in the finale against Cleveland, according to the Patriots' official game notes .

Veterans Harold Landry III and Dre'Mont Jones also occupy prominent positions in the Patriots' pass-rush rotation.

That left Luketa battling for a reserve role in a crowded position group. His NFL experience and special teams background made him a plausible candidate, but the Patriots evidently decided those traits were not enough to justify keeping him over a younger player with more developmental upside.

New England's decision also reinforces Vrabel's roster philosophy. Joining the team early and having prior NFL experience did not buy Luketa extra time. The Patriots signed him before making any other outside addition this offseason, evaluated him throughout the spring and summer, and still concluded they had better options.

For Luketa, the timing at least gives him an opportunity to find another team before the regular season begins. For the Patriots, his departure suggests their younger linebackers did enough to force a veteran out of the picture.

articles.title: Florida State football opens season with 34-17 win over Aggies
articles.summary: 'Noles gathered at Doak Campbell Stadium on Aug. 29 to witness FSU's first victory of the 2026 football season, demonstrating its strong defense.
articles.body:
Florida State football commenced the 2026 season with a home opener at Doak S. Campbell Stadium against the New Mexico State Aggies on Saturday, Aug. 29., where the Seminoles defeated the Aggies 34-17 in a roller coaster of a performance.

FSU started the game on defense after losing the coin toss. Despite the Aggies gaining some ground early on, the defense held strong. The crowd erupted after senior defensive back Quindarrius Jones intercepted a throw in the end zone to put the 'Noles on offense.

Following the turnover, the Garnet and Gold, led by fifth year quarterback Ashton Daniels, engineered a strong drive that brought them into the red zone. However, after Daniels was sacked on third and goal, Florida State was forced to settle for a field goal from senior kicker Gabe Panikowski to take an early 3-0 lead.

'Noles offense presents bright spots and room to improve

Later on in the first quarter, a screen pass from Daniels to senior running back Samuel Singleton Jr. set the Seminoles up inside the New Mexico State 10-yard line once again.

On third down, Daniels scored his first touchdown of the season as he evaded the blitz to give FSU a 10-0 lead early in the second quarter. However, New Mexico State bounced back with a touchdown of their own as New Mexico State junior quarterback Trey Hedden connected with senior receiver Brodie Malone-Bradford to cut the Aggies' deficit to three.

Despite two straight scoring drives to start the game, the 'Noles' offense stalled. A three-and-out followed by an interception from Daniels shifted the momentum to the Aggies midway through the second quarter.

"Obviously there's some plays we want to have back," Daniels said in the postgame press conference. "But I think we responded very well … we're gonna come in tomorrow, we're gonna watch … we're gonna learn from it and we're gonna make sure we get those things fixed."

On the other hand, the Garnet and Gold defense stymied the New Mexico State offense. A sack by fifth year linebacker Mikai Gbayor forced the Aggies' offense back, and they were soon forced to punt.

Florida State regained some momentum as Singleton caught a pass from Daniels for a touchdown with under a minute left in the half, putting the Seminoles ahead 17-7 going into the break.

Seminoles defense is a strongpoint early in the season

In the second half, FSU's defense picked up where it left off and kept the Aggies contained.

With less than three minutes left in the third quarter, Singleton extended the 'Noles' lead to 24-10 after a lengthy drive of over five minutes of game-time.

The Garnet and Gold defense remained strong in the latter half of the quarter, keeping the lethargic Aggies offense in their own territory and forcing them to punt as the game entered the fourth quarter.

With Florida State looking to protect its double-digit lead, the Seminoles leaned on the ground game. Sophomore running back Ousmane Kromah broke off a game-high 52-yard run that took FSU into New Mexico State territory. The 'Noles eventually settled for a field goal on the drive, extending their lead to 27-10. Kromah finished the game with 14 carries for 115 yards and a touchdown.

Facing a three-possession deficit, the Aggies did not relent. On second down at the Garnet and Gold's 34-yard line, Hedden tossed his second touchdown pass of the night as he attacked Florida State's middle safeties to cut the lead down to 27-17.

"I feel like we didn't play up to our standard," junior linebacker Chris Jones said postgame. "We just gotta come out faster, be more urgent, and then clean up the details."

Garnet and Gold hold on to secure perfect record

Florida State continued to fight back offensively. With less than five minutes left in the game, the Seminoles powered through with a 1-yard touchdown run from Kromah to bring the lead back to 17, and eventually finish the game with a 34-17 win to start the 2026 season 1-0.

"There's some good and bad that showed up," head coach Mike Norvell said in the postgame press conference. "Throughout the course of the game [there's] a lot of areas where we're gonna be able to grow and continue to push to get better."

FSU will play their next game at Doak S. Campbell Stadium against Southern Methodist University at 7:30 p.m. on Monday, Sep. 7.

articles.title: A draw in Cardiff still leaves unanswered questions
articles.summary: BBC Final Score's Laura Kenyon says despite their first Championship goals of the season, Sheffield United still have issues to resolve.
articles.body:
The Cardiff game probably left Sheffield United fans slightly puzzled about what to expect in the coming weeks. Boss Chris Wilder himself admitted he was left scratching his head at such an open and breathless game.

However, some encouragement emerged in the form of a first Championship goal of the new season.

It comes after a measly combined total of just four shots on target from the opening two league games. Questions loomed about where the goals would come from this season.

Some answers were found at Cardiff City Stadium.

Tom Cannon's successful penalty was his second goal in two games, having netted in the EFL Cup in midweek. A goal from open play was even more encouraging, with Callum O'Hare looking like one of Sheffield United's bigger attacking threats.

There was a cameo from Ben Brererton Diaz. The striker returned on loan for his third spell at the club in midweek, but will he be the prolific goalscorer of past Championship seasons?

Will Patrick Bamford step up to Wilder's call for more? He produced another quiet performance in Cardiff.

Blades fans will hope it does not take a third trip to south Wales to conjure up resolutions.

articles.title: New Orleans Saints waive 10 players on the eve of roster cuts deadline
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints began the difficult process of cutting down their roster before the NFL deadline by waiving 10 players on Saturday evening.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints began the difficult process of cutting down their roster before the NFL deadline by waiving 10 players on Saturday evening. All teams must meet the 53-man roster limit no later than 5 p.m. CT on Sunday, Aug. 30, and many of them have gotten a head start. You can keep up with all of the Saints' roster moves, trade rumors, and reported developments in our live tracker right here .

Most of the Saints' initial roster cuts were on the practice squad last year; that group includes wide receiver Ronnie Bell, safety Elliott Davison, quarterback Hunter Dekkers , and tight end Zaire Mitchell-Paden. Edge rusher Garrett Neson was briefly part of New Orleans' practice squad a year ago before moving on. Another wide receiver, Bub Means , spent the 2025 season on injured reserve after going down in the preseason. And offensive lineman Xavier Truss remained on the Saints' 53-man roster all season after being claimed off of waivers from the Denver Broncos .

A handful of other players have been waived without any previous experience in New Orleans: defensive tackle Brien Taylor Jr. and edge rusher Malakai Williams, both of whom tried out early in training camp and signed with the Saints after injuries sidelined starters like Cameron Jordan (for a month) and Bryan Bresee (for the year). They may have been brought in to maintain numbers and keep practice running smoothly, but they still got to wear the fleur-de-lis into a game at the Caesars Superdome. That matters.

All ten of these players will test the waiver wire, giving other teams an opportunity to claim them. If they go unclaimed, there may be room for them on the practice squad in New Orleans. We'll just have to wait and see if they stick around.

As reported by Sky Sport , the deal between Juventus and Tottenham for Pape Sarr is getting closer and closer to being finalized: a paid loan worth 3 million with an option to buy for 30 million, which can become an obligation under certain conditions.

The player is highly rated by Ricky Massara, who had wanted to sign him during his time at Milan: a deal that was impossible at the time.

Milan, Betis try to overtake in the race for Fofana

According to Fabrizio Romano , Galatasaray got Fofana's approval during the day yesterday, but other clubs are also making moves for the midfielder.

According to Daniele Longo , Real Betis are now the club in the strongest position for Fofana. The player would still prefer a move to the Premier League. According to MilanNews Lyon and Lille are also interested in him, although he does not want to return to France.

Inter, Kamaté heading to Atletico Madrid

Inter are wrapping up their outgoing transfer business: according to Matteo Moretto , Kamaté has agreed to join Atletico Madrid: a deal worth 2 million plus 30% of any future resale . He will initially play for the second team, coached by Fernando Torres.

The 2004-born player had come very close to joining Espanyol in this transfer window and had turned down an approach from Palermo.

Napoli, Zeballos reinstated to the squad

Exequiel Zeballos waited for Napoli all summer and may wait even longer: according to Argentine media, the player has returned to training with Boca after having been frozen out in recent weeks.

The transfer window is not over and Sevilla and Parma remain interested in him, but it cannot be ruled out that the player stays in Argentina and joins Napoli in January, as reported in recent days by Fabrizio Romano .

The Giallorossi would like to make an offer of a paid loan worth 5 million + an option to buy set at 30 million.

Lazio, Cancellieri and Dia on the way out

Boulaye Dia, meanwhile, is liked by Rennes: Lazio are confident they can sell him to Ligue 1, while the player has not yet approved the move.

Earlier today Nicolò Fagioli had liked an Instagram post criticizing Grosso's work in these first few months on the job. It was a gesture that had sparked thoughts of a rift, given the signing of Oulai for the same position.

Fagioli himself, however, wanted to explain everything in the comments under the post: "Calm down... I accidentally tapped it while scrolling. I'm not that stupid to think or do something like that for no reason. Let's not create unnecessary controversy now, there's no need" .

Dirk van Duijvenbode knocked out top seed Luke Humphries on Day Two at the Hungarian Darts Trophy, as Gary Anderson delivered a virtuoso performance in Budapest.

Van Duijvenbode ended his nine-match losing run against Humphries to book his place at Finals Day at the MVM Dome, maintaining his resurgent form in the process.

The World Matchplay semi-finalist rattled off four consecutive legs from 3-2 adrift to cap off a classy display, averaging 98 and conjuring up a spectacular 140 checkout in the closing stages of the contest.

"Luke is a phenomenal player, but I think I'm okay as well," quipped Van Duijvenbode – a three-time runner-up on the European Tour circuit.

"I'm happier in life at the moment. I've had a lot of struggles, but I feel better, life is better and I'm getting better now hopefully."

Van Duijvenbode will now go head-to-head with Rob Cross on Finals Day, after the former World Champion landed a 130 checkout to deny Luke Woodhouse in a compelling last-leg shoot-out.

Gian van Veen and Michael van Gerwen also advanced on a bumper day of round two action at the MVM Dome, courtesy of victories over Nandor Major and James Hurrell respectively.Van Veen pinned 67% of his attempts at double and converted a sublime 167 finish to whitewash Major, while Van Gerwen overturned a 3-1 deficit in sealing a comeback win against Hurrell.

Scottish icon Anderson marked his return to big stage action in style, averaging 105.27 in his 6-2 thumping of Krzysztof Ratajski – halting the Pole's bid for back-to-back European Tour titles.

Ross Smith also registered a ton-plus average to dispatch William O'Connor by the same scoreline, and his reward is a tie with Jonny Clayton, who ran out a 6-3 winner against Hungary's Laszlo Kadar.Nathan Aspinall opened his title challenge with a battling 6-4 win against Ryan Joyce, landing five 180s to set up a blockbuster showdown against Van Gerwen for a place in the last eight.

Stephen Bunting will lock horns with Anderson in another intriguing tussle, after the Liverpudlian began his campaign with a comprehensive 6-1 win at the expense of Finland's Jonas Masalin.

Chris Dobey launched a terrific fightback from 4-0 down to deny Tom Sykes in a decider, and his next assignment will be a tussle against sixth seed Josh Rock, who whitewashed a struggling Joe Cullen in the evening's finale.

Jermaine Wattimena overcame Andrew Gilding in a hard-fought affair to earn a showdown against Van Veen, while Keane Barry swept aside Madars Razma to reach the last 16 of a European Tour event for the first time since April 2023.

articles.title: Former TCU safety Jacob Fields charged with aggravated assault on teammate
articles.summary: Former TCU safety Jacob Fields was charged with aggravated assault, per court records, for a fight that got him previously removed from the team.
articles.body:
Former TCU safety Jacob Fields turned himself in to authorities and was charged after allegedly striking former teammate Dozie Ezukanma earlier this month.

According to Tarrant County court records, Fields was booked Sunday, Aug. 30, on a charge of aggravated assault causing serious bodily injury. No bond amount for Fields was posted at the time this story was published.

The former Horned Frogs safety was dismissed from the program on Tuesday, Aug. 18 for an unspecified violation of team rules.

"Due to a violation of team rules, Jacob Fields has been removed from our roster and will not be a member of our team football team moving forward," a TCU spokesman told ESPN in a statement on Aug. 18.

Bill Belichick, UNC football open Year 2 with win over TCU in Ireland

The Fort Worth Star-Telegram initially reported Fields' altercation, reporting it occurred with a teammate on offense. It was noted in the TCU crime and fire log as having occurred 1:30 p.m. local time Thursday, Aug. 13. It was then not reported until 2:29 p.m. the following day, four days before TCU announced his dismissal from the team.

TCU would go on to revoke credentials from a Fort Worth Star-Telegram reporter for reporting on the situation just a few days before the Horned Frogs ' Week 0 opener in Dublin against North Carolina.

"It was something that was certainly out of character for the team and the young man that was involved," TCU coach Sonny Dykes said earlier this week in Dublin when asked about the matter. "Look, you got 110 football players. I mean, things happen sometimes. You've got to find ways to move through them, and, man, these young kids are resilient.

"It's like anything else, when something bad happens, it becomes a teaching moment. And so we were able to teach our players, and I think the guys are better off from having gone through it."

Fields, a three-star transfer from Louisiana Tech, was projected to be a starter for the Horned Frogs after earning Conference USA Defensive Player of the Year in 2025. He finished with 91 total tackles, five broken-up passes and three interceptions, two of which were returned for a score, last season at Louisiana Tech.

TCU dropped its season opener, 15-10, on Saturday, Aug. 29, in Ireland to North Carolina in the Aer Lingus College Football Classic.

articles.title: ESPN grades Falcons' trade for Bears DT Gervon Dexter
articles.summary: ESPN declares Falcons the winner of trade for Bears DT Gervon Dexter
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons swung a trade with the Chicago Bears on Sunday morning, sending cornerback Clark Phillips III and a fifth-round draft pick to the Bears in exchange for defensive tackle Gervon Dexter.

Atlanta was fairly thin at defensive tackle, even after trading for former Jaguars DT Maason Smith earlier in the offseason. Dexter is a major upgrade for the Falcons, and his presence should bring out the best in the team's young pass-rushers.

On paper, it looks like Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham got a great deal from his mentor Ryan Pace. Even ESPN seemed to agree that Atlanta got the best of Chicago. Ben Solak gave the Falcons an A-minus grade, while the Bears received "C" for the trade.

"This a good get for the Falcons, who needed defensive tackle help worse than perhaps any other team in the league. Free agent addition Da'Shawn Hand has missed most of training camp with a leg injury, leaving only bottom-of-the-roster contributors to fill the starting spot besides Brandon Dorlus. In Dexter, the Falcons grab a player big enough to play the nose next to Dorlus, but with enough power and pass-rush technique to still matter on passing downs. Dexter had a pressure rate of 10.5% last season by NFL Next Gen Stat's charting, 11th among all defensive tackles and well above the league average for defensive tackles (7.4%)." - Ben Solak, ESPN

Dexter, 24, recorded 44 tackles (21 solo) and six sacks for the Bears last season. Over his three years in Chicago, the former second-round pick has racked up 115 tackles (57 solo), 13.5 sacks and 42 QB hits. Dexter projects to start at nose tackle for the Falcons in 2026.

So why did the Bears give up Dexter? After all, it's tough to find good interior defensive linemen, and especially those who can push the pocket to create sacks.

Solak goes on to say that the deal had to do with Dexter being in the final year of his contract, but even if the Falcons don't re-sign Dexter, they will still be awarded a compensatory pick.

"Dexter is on a contract year, which is one of the reasons he was available for a cheap return. If he has a good year in Atlanta, the Falcons might consider extending him… but they might also let him walk for a compensatory pick that replaces (or improves upon) the fifth-rounder they lost in letting him go." - Solak

The Falcons have more work to do, though. The NFL's 53-man roster deadline is Sunday evening at 6 p.m. ET. The team has already trimmed 11 players but must cut 26 more before today's deadline. Follow along with each more using our Falcons roster cuts tracker !

articles.title: UFC Shanghai, The Morning After: A Crack In The Dagestan Dominance
articles.summary: Song Yadong beat the odds in his UFC Shanghai main event battle versus Umar Nurmagomedov. I’m not just talking about the betting odds, which pegged “The Kung...
articles.body:
Song Yadong beat the odds in his UFC Shanghai main event battle versus Umar Nurmagomedov .

I'm not just talking about the betting odds , which pegged "The KungFu Kid" as somewhere between a 4-1 and 7-1 underdog depending on your site of choice. There was also historical precedent going against Yadong, who had faltered in his previous opportunities to step up against the highest echelon of contenders like Petr Yan , Sean O'Malley , and Cory Sandhagen .

Even larger than that trend is both the historic and contemporary dominance of the Nurmagomedov clan. Russian wrestling is currently the most dominant force in mixed martial arts (MMA), and that trajectory was paved by Khabib Nurmagomedov . His protege, Islam Makhachev , is the best pound-for-pound fighter alive right now, a double champion with defenses at both weight classes. Khabib's cousins, Umar and Usman, are not yet UFC champions, but they're winning all the time and showing world-class skill in the process. Last year, Umar Nurmagomedov came within a single round of dethroning Merab Dvalishvili , and he's already beaten two top contenders since then in his would-be rebound back to gold.

Outside of the Nurmagomedov inner circle itself, Russian wrestlers like Khamzat Chimaev and Movsar Evloev are the cream of the crop. The stats and trends are clear: we're in the midst of a dynasty of Russian wrestlers who can pin the best fighters on the planet a very high percentage of the time.

When one of them loses, it's a shock, and it's worth analyzing further.

Song Yadong's ability to strategize and adjust to his opponents has been a point of critique in the past, but he arrived in the Octagon well-prepared to challenge Nurmagomedov. At distance, Yadong was actively kicking and choosing smart targets that are difficult to counter with wrestling shots. Though kicking a wrestler always carries risk — and indeed, Nurmagomedov's sole takedown of the fight came from a caught calf kick — it's a necessary gamble. Umar, like Islam and Usman, is a great kicker himself. A fighter who just gives away the range battle without even trying to participate in fear of the takedown has conceded another realm of the fight to his opponent, making it even more difficult to build success.

The other immediately apparent adjustment from Yadong was to hammer the body. Several times in the opening round, Yadong flashed a jab and then stepped deep into his right hand aimed at the chest. He landed cleanly on several occasions, and the benefits are numerous. A straight punch to the body is nearly impossible to shoot through — that's how Nurmagomedov ended up getting knocked out in the end. Even if a fighter isn't counting on that perfect KO connection, however, we're talking about fighters who cut a lot of weight and maintain an exhaustive style.

Attacking their gas tank is always a good choice.

Finally, Yadong had a strategy for escaping from bottom position. Against a truly top-notch wrestler, the takedown is a matter of when, not if. Yadong has an incredibly athletic sprawl, but fighting in a kickboxing stance will naturally land you out of position and vulnerable to being grounded at some point regardless of one's strong hips.

When Nurmagomedov took down Yadong, he wasn't able to rest. He fought off a guillotine, then all of his considerable muscles were flexing merely to keep Yadong in guard. Yadong didn't hold his opponent to him in top position like Dricus du Plessis or accept bottom position a la Jack de la Maddalena . As soon as Nurmagomedov wasn't actively flexing him in place — which, again, is a drain on the gas tank — Yadong was entering on a deep half guard and using that position to create scrambles and stand.

When the two returned to their feet with a minute remaining in the first, both men were moving a little slower. Yadong was forced to expend energy himself to make Nurmagomedov work, but in the process, he had brought the fight back to his desired venue. As a result, Yadong could go back to targeting the body and calf, while Nurmagomedov was forced to find another takedown. His first attempt was met with a sprawl, and the second ran him directly into a fight-ending right hand.

For the first time, a member of the immediate Nurmagomedov family was knocked out cold, and it happened just two weeks after Makhachev was pushed to the brink by Ian Garry, who also emphasized attritional damage and smart scrambling in his bid to upset the champion.

Are we at the end of Russian wrestling dominance? Is everybody going to start knocking out Nurmagomedovs? Of course not. Yadong is a remarkable fighter in his own right with nearly unmatched physical gifts. That said, as we see more consistency in what works against the currently dominant style, there will be more upsets and trials for even the best fighters Dagestan has to offer.

articles.title: UNC’s Bill Belichick Gives ESPN the Silent Treatment on the Field (Video)
articles.summary: Bill Belichick came to Ireland looking to change the narrative around his second UNC season, and he left with a different kind of headline. North Carolina op...
articles.body:
Bill Belichick came to Ireland looking to change the narrative around his second UNC season, and he left with a different kind of headline.

North Carolina opened its season against TCU, the same team that handed the Tar Heels a lopsided 48-14 defeat last September. This time the storyline shifted before the final whistle. A new moment involving Belichick and a sideline reporter has fans talking for reasons that go beyond the scoreboard.

Bill Belichick Snubs ESPN Reporter In Halftime Walk

As North Carolina Tar Heels and TCU headed toward their locker rooms at halftime inside Dublin's Aviva Stadium, an ESPN reporter stepped into Belichick's path with a microphone, hoping for his read on the first two quarters. The 74-year-old coach did not slow down.

He kept walking toward the tunnel while she matched his pace beside him, and neither one raised their voice. There was no shove and no shouting match, just a coach who chose silence over a sound bite.

Betting account Bet105 later posted a nine-second clip of the exchange on X, calling it a clash in the caption, and the post passed one million views within hours. A closer look at the footage shows something closer to a snub than a confrontation.

The reporter's postgame update leaned entirely on comments from TCU's sideline, since Belichick offered nothing during the walk.

Tar Heels went on to win 15-10, avenging last season's 48-14 loss to the same opponent in Chapel Hill.

Once the game wrapped, Quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. told ESPN, "Hats off to the defense. They kept us in it the whole game. Big-time stops in the fourth quarter."

A late penalty on TCU, its 11th infraction of the day, sealed the result in the final minutes. However, the scoreboard was not the only storyline Belichick carried into Ireland.

Off-Field Turmoil Still Follows Bill Belichick At UNC

Saturday's win offered a rare bright spot in a stretch that started under a cloud. General manager Michael Lombardi remains on paid administrative leave following a human resources complaint connected to an NCAA investigation into the program .

Defensive coordinator Steve Belichick has been away from the team on medical leave since early August, with no set return date, leaving his father to call the defense himself in Dublin.

That kind of turmoil does not stay contained to the practice field. It followed Belichick into national coverage all preseason. Paul Finebaum called Belichick a "grouch" and a "bully" on ESPN's First Take just days before the TCU game, and the line stuck.

A 15-10 win will not silence that chorus, but it buys the program a little breathing room heading into September.

Tar Heels sits 1-0 for the first time in the Belichick era and gets a bye before hosting East Tennessee State on September 12. TCU drops to 0-1 and returns to Fort Worth to face Grambling State the same day, looking to reset quickly.

articles.title: Cardinals QB coach Matt Schaub called plays in preseason finale
articles.summary: The Cardinals piled up 492 yards of offense with Matty Schaub calling plays.
articles.body:
Yes, it was backups against backups, but the Arizona Cardinals exploded for 492 yards in Friday night's loss to the Green Bay Packers , averaging 6.2 yards per their 79 plays, totaling 27 first downs, converting 9-of-15 third-down opportunities and controlling the ball for 37:31.

In the first half, the total was 323 yards on 42 plays (7.7 average) with 16 first downs and time of possession of 20:01.

They did all that with quarterbacks coach Matt Schaub calling the plays in his first season as an NFL coach. Schaub played the position for 17 seasons, ending in 2020, and the closest he had come to coaching was as a football analyst with the Atlanta Falcons in 2023.

Earlier in training camp, Schaub said "I'm just a football guy," when asked what got him back in the game full-time.

"There's something in it (that) just kept drawing me back," he added. "When I finished up, I wanted to step away and be a husband and father (to four daughters). My family gave up so much time for the game for me when I was playing that I wanted to go try something new. I wanted to go do something different. But something kept tugging at me to come back and this opportunity came up.

"Knowing him (head coach Mike LaFleur) from years gone by and his brother and just that tree of coaching; just something I couldn't pass up this opportunity. It's just something that kept calling me back and my wife was super-supportive of this decision and my family. So couldn't be more thankful for them."

Explaining the decision to have Schaub call plays, LaFleur said, "I was always given ops when I wasn't a play-caller yet. There's not only developing players, but there's developing staff as well. And so when I put it out there for him to see if he wanted to do it, he was ecstatic about it. It was cool."

LaFleur said what Schaub does best in his main role is "he brings it back to the foundational level and he's right by doing that. The cadence, how you operate, where your eyes need to go, rhythm, timing, accuracy. All those things are so awesome for our quarterbacks to hear because it's just the same every day. He's steady. He's never going to be too high, he's never gonna be too low. He's done it at this level and so there's obviously going to be respect."

As for what he brings to his style as a former player, Schaub explained, "I know what they're going through both mentally with the playbook, with the plan, with adjustments. So, I can relate to the position they're in and I can relate to how things happen on the field because it's easy when you have a clicker in your hand in an air-conditioned room to coach guys on what should happen or give them attaboys. I know that, but what's realistic?

"Where are your eyes? Where are the fundamentals in the details? Subtle nuances that if you hadn't played the position sometimes you might miss. And that's where I think my experience might be able be a benefit to them."

Meanwhile, it turns out Schaub wasn't the only one in the game other than the coach who normally calls plays.

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur revealed after the game that starting quarterback Jordan Love did the duty in the second half.

LaFleur said, "I was kind of messing with him before the game. I just went up to him, so it's not like he had time to prep, and I was like 'Hey, you want to call it in the second half?' and he was like 'Sure, yeah I'll do it,' and he did it and he did an outstanding job."

The head coach added it "was pretty cool just to hear his demeanor on the headset, how calm, cool and collected he was throughout the entire game, especially in those critical moments. It's not a surprise to me because that's what we see on the field too."

Then, asked if Love was calmer than he is, LaFleur said, "A lot calmer. I think I learned something from him today."
